description: Area 52 is developing FIREWATCH for the “Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots” challenge. We are investigating where and when MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections agree or differ, using satellite data analysis and visualizations. I’m building the Python/Colab workflow and welcome teammates interested in Earth science, remote sensing, data analysis, statistics, visualization, and science communication.
summary:
FIREWATCH is an exploratory research prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge of harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS active fire observations.

The project investigates whether spatial and temporal disagreements between satellite fire detections may contain useful information about Earth observation patterns. Using NASA FIRMS data from the Cerrado region of Brazil during the 2025 dry season, FIREWATCH applies data processing, temporal pairing, spatial aggregation, neighborhood analysis, and statistical testing.

The project explores alternative analytical metrics, null models, and spatial resolution sensitivity to better understand satellite observation differences. Its goal is to support transparent and reproducible analysis, not to claim operational fire prediction or validated detection accuracy.
